answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by rationing trust through scarce, slowly replenishing endorsements. An established agent may vouch for a newcomer only by signing an endorsement, a quill mark that stays attached to both names, and each endorser holds only a few slots that refill over a long horizon. A newcomer gathers standing from a meadow of independent endorsers, never from one sponsor alone. Each fake identity therefore consumes scarce slots from many agents, and if a vouched identity cheats, its endorsers lose slots permanently, so manufacturing identities gets costlier with scale.
